title: Remote MCPs: What we learned from shipping — John Welsh, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic built a centralized MCP gateway so internal LLM-backed services connect to any internal or external tool via one `connect(url)` call, with OAuth, rate limiting, and observability handled once at the gateway. The core lesson is standardizing the plumbing layer and making the right path the easiest path ('pit of success').

takeaways.technique: Centralized MCP gateway as single ingress/egress
takeaways.what_they_do: One shared service exposes a single `connect(url)` call returning an MCP SDK session; URL-based routing reaches internal or external servers identically, and credentials/OAuth are managed centrally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we designed a service which is just a piece of shared infrastructure called the MCP gateway that provides a single point of entry

takeaways.technique: Gateway-level credential custody and policy enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents pass an internal user/org ID (signed token) to the gateway; the gateway holds stored OAuth credentials and injects bearer tokens, so individual services never touch user credentials or open outbound connections.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't really want all of those services to be going and accessing user credentials

takeaways.technique: Standardized message format as an interception point
takeaways.what_they_do: Because all tool traffic is MCP JSON in one stream, they hook processors for tool execution, tool definitions, and resources centrally — enabling content classification, banning malicious servers, and audit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because it's MCP, all of your messages are in a standardized format. So it's really easy to hook into that stream

takeaways.technique: Transport is a small implementation detail
takeaways.what_they_do: They show the same MCP client session fed by websockets, gRPC, Unix sockets, even IMAP — the transport is a few lines piping read/write streams into the SDK.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP is really just JSON streams and how you pipe those streams around your infrastructure is a small implementation detail

takeaways.technique: Pit of success: make the right path the easiest path
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately made the sanctioned integration path a one-line import so engineers naturally do the right thing rather than being told to.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you make the right thing to do, the easiest thing to do, then everyone in your org kind of falls into it
